headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk: kotaemon’s web/RAG ingestion can feed plano’s OpenAI-compatible routing without verification, while both have broad egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents/HTML/MHTML and exposes a web UI, while plano routes chat completions through an OpenAI-compatible gateway. That creates a plausible default path where attacker-controlled content from A is passed into B as instructions. No shared filesystem is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF kotaemon content is forwarded into plano prompts without sanitization
IF plano preserves raw upstream text in routed messages
mitigations: Add a prompt-injection filter before forwarding A outputs to B
Strip HTML/MHTML and hidden text from A outputs
Require a human review step for any instruction-like content
Log and block messages containing tool directives
requires-engineering: add provenance tags across the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and broad document types, and plano sends traffic to an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint with broad egress. If both are used on the same sensitive workspace, data can flow from A into B’s outbound requests. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same documents or transcripts
IF plano forwards prompt context containing A-ingested secrets to its upstream API
mitigations: Separate the workspaces for A and B
Remove secrets from A inputs before routing
Disable upstream calls for sensitive jobs
Review outbound payloads for API keys
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data, while plano uses config.yaml and does not support multiple instances. If they share a mutable directory or deployment state, concurrent writes can conflict. The profiles do not show a shared lock or orchestrator, so the safest reading is a default-capable conflict at medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path or config volume
IF no external lock serializes updates
mitigations: Place each agent in its own directory
Make config.yaml read-only during runtime
Run only one writer at a time
Back up mutable state before changes
requires-engineering: add file locking or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon produces retrieved answers from documents and citations, and plano is an AI gateway that can route those outputs onward. If plano treats A’s text as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions. Because no verification layer is documented, I choose medium and not low.
conditions: IF plano forwards kotaemon-generated answers without validation
IF downstream consumers act on routed text as factual
mitigations: Require citation checks before forwarding
Add a confidence threshold for routed answers
Insert a human approval step for high-impact outputs
Compare A outputs against source documents
requires-engineering: implement structured verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon touches API keys and customer-support documents, while plano stores logs/metrics/traces and routes prompts to an external chat endpoint. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch for sensitive support data, even though the profiles do not specify jurisdictions or certifications. I therefore keep this at medium.
conditions: IF customer-support documents or secrets are sent through plano
IF plano retains logs or traces longer than the source system
mitigations: Minimize sensitive fields before routing
Set short retention on logs and traces
Document data-flow boundaries for support data
Exclude API keys from prompts
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
